text:
maya: Quick follow-up from the RFC — can we compress the rollout hint blob to save per-request header size? thinking about tenants with long variant lists. :thinking:

devon: Are you proposing a wire-compressed field or a separate encoded header?

maya: Separate header + versioned flag. e.g. `X-Rollout-Hint` (v1 plain JSON) and `X-Rollout-Hint-V2` (base64+gzip). Server would accept both and expand to canonical object internally.

sam: That could work. Main tradeoff is client compatibility: older clients will ignore V2 header unless we also send V1. Doubling traffic if we keep both.

anna: Do we have metrics on header length distribution? If only rare tenants exceed limits maybe we only enable compression via opt-in?

maya: I pulled a sample: ~95th percentile is ~1.4KB, tail hits 18KB for large custom rollout rules. Some CDNs clamp header sizes. So not rare for big tenants.

devon: OK. If we do V2 binary header, we need a clear upgrade path: 1) API produces V2, 2) server side expands, 3) downstream services consume canonical metadata. Clients should keep sending V1 for N weeks during rollout.

sam: Also think about caching: many caches are keyed on headers. If we change header format, cache hit ratio could plummet. Maybe put the heavy blob into a token-like pointer: `X-Rollout-Blob-Token: <id>` and store blob in a fast KV with TTL. Clients get token via control-plane API.

maya: I like the token idea for public-hosted customers, but for Dedicated/Private that might be harder (no control-plane access). We need an in-protocol solution that works offline.

anna: What about hybrid? If tenant is on hosted, server issues token and sends token header. If private/dedicated, use V2 compressed header. We document both and prefer token when available.

devon: Edge case: function routing and tool-calling components will need the expanded object synchronously. Expansion cost matters. We should make expansion lazy and cache expanded blobs keyed by a stable hash.

sam: Good point. Use a content-hash field in header, e.g. `rollout-hint-sha256: abc123`, so services can look up expanded version in cache and avoid decompressing repeatedly.

maya: Proposed plan: 1) define V2 header (base64+gzip) schema and stable canonicalization rules; 2) add optional `X-Rollout-Blob-Token` for hosted only; 3) include `Rollout-Hash` header for idempotent cache keys; 4) servers accept V1/V2/Token precedence: Token > V2 > V1; 5) migration window: 6 weeks normal, 2 weeks beta.

devon: Need to add telemetry: counts of V1/V2/Token, decompression errors, expansion latency, cache hit ratio. Also a fallback policy if decompress fails (reject vs accept best-effort).

anna: For schema changes we should include a `schema_version` inside the payload (not only the header version) to allow additive fields like `affinity_weights` and `soft_expiry`.

sam: Agree. Also validate that compressed payloads still have readable `schema_version` after decompression; if not, log and reject with 400 so clients can self-correct.

maya: One compatibility worry: some proxies strip unknown headers or base64 characters. We should encode V2 to URL-safe base64 and keep size under common proxy limits (~16KB).

devon: Can we add an option to move large arrays into a URL (signed blob) that the caller fetches? That introduces another roundtrip though.

maya: Too expensive for hot requests. I'd rather rely on token or compressed header.

release-bot: Canary rollout scheduled: `rollout-metadata-v2` -> staging at 2024-11-02T03:00Z (auto-canary 10%).

anna: For testing: we need unit tests for canonicalization, fuzz tests for random variant lists, and an integration test hitting a staging proxy to ensure no stripping.

devon: I'll draft a small RFC follow-up with examples and a migration checklist. Need owners from eng-runtime and eng-platform.

maya: Owners: devon (runtime), anna (platform), sam (telemetry). I'll add the draft to the RFC thread and link the canary. Thanks all. :tada:
